overview: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America and the only one without a Caribbean coastline. Its capital and largest city is San Salvador. El Salvador became independent from Spain in 1821, at first as part of a Central American federation. It uses the US dollar, and in 2021 it became the first country to adopt Bitcoin as legal money.

geography.text: El Salvador faces the Pacific Ocean. A line of volcanoes runs across the country, and earthquakes are common. Between the volcanic highlands and the coastal plain lies a central plateau where most people live, and the Lempa is its main river.

history.text: El Salvador was home to the Pipil people before the Spanish conquest. It became independent in 1821 and was dominated for a long time by coffee-growing landowners. A civil war from 1980 to 1992 killed around 75,000 people and ended with peace accords.

events.title: Independence
events.text: El Salvador becomes independent from Spain.

events.title: La Matanza
events.text: Thousands of peasants are killed after an uprising.

events.title: Football War
events.text: A short war with Honduras follows World Cup qualifying matches.

events.title: Peace accords
events.text: A peace agreement ends twelve years of civil war.

government.text: El Salvador is a presidential republic. Since 2019 President Nayib Bukele has led a tough crackdown on gangs, with tens of thousands of people imprisoned under a state of emergency. Murders have fallen sharply, but human rights groups have criticised mass arrests and the weakening of courts. A 2021 court ruling allowed him to run for a second term, which he won in 2024.

economy.text: El Salvador uses the US dollar. Money sent home by Salvadorans living abroad, mostly in the United States, makes up around a fifth of the economy. Clothing, coffee and sugar are exports. In 2021 it became the first country to make Bitcoin legal tender, a step it largely reversed in 2025.

culture.text: El Salvador is the smallest country in Central America. Pupusas, thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans or pork, are the national dish and have their own national day. Joya de Cerén, a Maya village buried by a volcano around 600 AD, is called the 'Pompeii of the Americas'.

items.title: Pupusas
items.text: Stuffed corn tortillas, celebrated on National Pupusa Day.

items.title: Joya de Cerén
items.text: A farming village buried by volcanic ash, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. El Salvador has played at two World Cups, in 1970 and 1982. Surfing is growing on its Pacific coast, which hosted the World Surfing Games.

didYouKnow: El Salvador has more than 20 volcanoes.
